newsitem.title: UK: Well supported dlr ends slightly higher in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Well supported dlr ends slightly higher in Europe.

text.p: The dollar closed higher against the mark and the yen, supported by buoyant U.S. asset markets and receding fears about a delay to the start of European monetary union, traders said.
The U.S. currency found solid bids on a dip below 1.70 marks. Sentiment remained bullish after Wall Street closed at a fresh record high on Monday and got off to another firm start today.

"The dollar is rangebound but there's a feeling that there's more upside to come, so it's really well supported on dips," said a senior trader at a German bank here. "It's just taking a breather after its rise above 1.72 marks on Friday."
The yield gap between 10-year German and U.S. bonds widened back above 100 basis points, adding support to the dollar.
At 1540 GMT, the dollar was at 1.7060/65 marks versus 1.7025/35 late on Monday and an overnight low at 1.6975. Dollar/yen was at 121.85/95 from 121.69/74.
Earlier comments on Tuesday by Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler, who said there was no case for a German interest rate move either up or down, failed to move the dollar.

News that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had reshuffled his cabinet prompted limited kneejerk dollar buying against the mark but had little net effect. Mark support eroded further after a slew of comments from Bundesbank council members late on Monday all said the single European currency should be launched on time. Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria allow for small deviations from the 3.0 percent deficit/output ratio and EMU could take place as planned in 1999 without softening the wording of the treaty. Bundesbanker Guntram Palm, meantime, said speculation of an EMU was "totally misplaced" and he said he expects a majority of EU states to meet the criteria on time. His colleague Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher and President of the European Monetary Institute Alexandre Lamfalussy also stressed that small deviations from Maastricht's "reference values" were allowed if the leeway is used sparingly.
A speech by Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse at 1800 GMT will also be eyed.

"The economic fundamentals and interest rate outlook as well as the strength of the Dow still all point to a higher dollar, while the Bundesbank are clearly now acting together to calm market fears of an EMU delay," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. Against the yen, the dollar recovered off an overnight low at 121.25 yen, hit on news of a robust 11.8 percent rise in Japanese machinery orders in January and after the benchmark three-month certificate of deposit rate rose to 0.55 percent, the highest since last August. Some dealers said dollar/yen caught a bid and retested the 122 yen level in afternoon trade here on reports of an explosion at a Japanese nuclear plant.
"The dollar/yen rate blipped up towards 122 as the headlines came up on the wires but the net effect was really marginal," the German bank trader said.
